sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya rājā daśarathaḥ sutam bharataṃ kekayīputram abravīd raghunandanaḥ
english: Now, after some time had passed, king Daśaratha, that joy of the Raghu line, spoke to his son Bharata, the son of Kaikeyī.

sanskrit: ayaṃ kekayarājasya putro vasati putraka tvāṃ netum āgato vīra yudhājin mātulas tava
english: "My son, this man who is staying here is the son of the king of the Kekayas — your maternal uncle Yudhājit has come, O hero, to take you away."

sanskrit: śrutvā daśarathasyaitad bharataḥ kekayīsutaḥ gamanāyābhicakrāma śatrughnasahitas tadā
english: Having heard this from Daśaratha, Bharata, son of Kaikeyī, prepared to depart, accompanied by Śatrughna.

sanskrit: āpṛcchya pitaraṃ śūro rāmaṃ cākliṣṭakāriṇam mātṝṃś cāpi naraśreṣṭhaḥ śatrughnasahito yayau
english: Taking leave of his father, and of Rāma who never wearied in action, and of his mothers as well, that best of men, the valiant Bharata, departed together with Śatrughna.

sanskrit: yudhājit prāpya bharataṃ saśatrughnaṃ praharṣitaḥ svapuraṃ prāviśad vīraḥ pitā tasya tutoṣa ha
english: Yudhājit, overjoyed at receiving Bharata along with Śatrughna, that hero entered his own city, and his father was greatly pleased.

sanskrit: sa tatra nyavasad bhrātrā saha satkārasatkṛtaḥ mātulenāśvapatinā putrasnehena lālitaḥ
english: There Bharata dwelt together with his brother, honoured with great hospitality, and fondly indulged by his maternal uncle Aśvapati with a father's affection.

sanskrit: tatrāpi nivasantau tau tarpyamāṇau ca kāmataḥ bhrātarau smaratāṃ vīrau vṛddhaṃ daśarathaṃ nṛpam
english: Even while dwelling there and being satisfied in every desire, the two heroic brothers kept remembering the aged king Daśaratha.

sanskrit: rājāpi tau mahātejāḥ sasmāra proṣitau sutau ubhau bharataśatrughnau mahendravaruṇopamau
english: The king too, of great majesty, remembered his two sons who were away — both Bharata and Śatrughna, comparable to Mahendra and Varuṇa.

sanskrit: sarva eva tu tasyeṣṭāś catvāraḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ svaśarīrād vinirvṛttāś catvāra iva bāhavaḥ
english: Yet all four of his sons, those bulls among men, were dear to him alike, as though they were four arms issuing from his own body.

sanskrit: teṣām api mahātejā rāmo ratikaraḥ pituḥ svayambhūr iva bhūtānāṃ babhūva guṇavattaraḥ
english: Yet among them all, the great-spirited Rāma, who gave delight to his father, excelled in virtues, as the Self-born Brahmā excels among all beings.

sanskrit: gate ca bharate rāmo lakṣmaṇaś ca mahābalaḥ pitaraṃ devasaṃkāśaṃ pūjayām āsatus tadā
english: After Bharata had departed, Rāma and the mighty Lakṣmaṇa honoured their father, who was like unto a god.

sanskrit: pitur ājñāṃ puraskṛtya paurakāryāṇi sarvaśaḥ cakāra rāmo dharmātmā priyāṇi ca hitāni ca
english: Placing his father's command foremost, Rāma, whose soul was set on righteousness, carried out all the duties toward the citizens — whatever was pleasing and whatever was beneficial.

sanskrit: mātṛbhyo mātṛkāryāṇi kṛtvā paramayantritaḥ gurūṇāṃ gurukāryāṇi kāle kāle 'nvavaikṣata
english: With the utmost self-restraint he performed the duties owed to his mothers, and at each proper time he attended to the duties owed to his teachers.

sanskrit: evaṃ daśarathaḥ prīto brāhmaṇā naigamās tathā rāmasya śīlavṛttena sarve viṣayavāsinaḥ
english: By Rāma's character and conduct, Daśaratha was pleased, as were the brāhmaṇas, the townspeople, and all the inhabitants of the kingdom.

sanskrit: sa hi nityaṃ praśāntātmā mṛdupūrvaṃ ca bhāṣate ucyamāno 'pi paruṣaṃ nottaraṃ pratipadyate
english: For he was ever tranquil of soul and spoke with gentle words first; even when addressed harshly, he returned no harsh reply.

sanskrit: kathaṃ cid upakāreṇa kṛtenaikena tuṣyati na smaraty apakārāṇāṃ śatam apy ātmavattayā
english: He was pleased by even a single service however slight, and through the mastery of his own self he did not remember even a hundred injuries done to him.

sanskrit: śīlavṛddhair jñānavṛddhair vayovṛddhaiś ca sajjanaiḥ kathayann āsta vai nityam astrayogyāntareṣv api
english: He was ever in conversation with good men who were advanced in conduct, knowledge, and age, even in the intervals between his exercises in archery.

sanskrit: kalyāṇābhijanaḥ sādhur adīnaḥ satyavāg ṛjuḥ vṛddhair abhivinītaś ca dvijair dharmārthadarśibhiḥ
english: He was of noble birth, virtuous, undepressed in spirit, truthful in speech, upright, and well-trained by elder twice-born men who understood righteousness and expediency.

sanskrit: dharmārthakāmatattvajñaḥ smṛtimān pratibhāvanān laukike samayācare kṛtakalpo viśāradaḥ
english: He understood the true nature of dharma, artha, and kāma; he was endowed with memory and swift wit; he was well-versed and expert in worldly convention and social conduct.

sanskrit: śāstrajñaś ca kṛtajñaś ca puruṣāntarakovidaḥ yaḥ pragrahānugrahayor yathānyāyaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ
english: He was learned in the śāstras and grateful for benefits received; he was skilled in reading the characters of men, and discerning in the proper exercise of restraint and favour.

sanskrit: āyakarmaṇy upāyajñaḥ saṃdṛṣṭavyayakarmavit śraiṣṭhyaṃ śāstrasamūheṣu prāpto vyāmiśrakeṣv api
english: He understood the means for raising revenue, and was knowledgeable about the workings of expenditure; he had attained eminence among the whole body of sciences, including the mixed branches of learning.

sanskrit: arthadharmau ca saṃgṛhya sukhatantro na cālasaḥ vaihārikāṇāṃ śilpānāṃ vijñātārthavibhāgavit
english: He grasped both artha and dharma together, was devoted to his own ease yet never indolent; he understood the principles and divisions of the practical arts.

sanskrit: ārohe vinaye caiva yukto vāraṇavājinām dhanurvedavidāṃ śreṣṭho loke 'tirathasaṃmataḥ
english: He was accomplished in the mounting and training of elephants and horses; he was the foremost among those learned in the science of archery, and acknowledged as an atiratha — a supreme chariot warrior — in the world.

sanskrit: abhiyātā prahartā ca senānayaviśāradaḥ apradhṛṣyaś ca saṃgrāme kruddhair api surāsuraiḥ
english: He was a bold attacker and a powerful striker, skilled in the movement of armies, and unconquerable in battle even by the wrath of gods and asuras alike.

sanskrit: anasūyo jitakrodho na dṛpto na ca matsarī na cāvamantā bhūtānāṃ na ca kālavaśānugaḥ
english: He was free from envy, had conquered anger, was not arrogant, not jealous, did not belittle any being, and was not enslaved by the force of circumstance.

sanskrit: evaṃ śreṣṭhair guṇair yuktaḥ prajānāṃ pārthivātmajaḥ saṃmatas triṣu lokeṣu vasudhāyāḥ kṣamāguṇaiḥ buddhyā bṛhaspates tulyo vīryeṇāpi śacīpateḥ
english: Thus endowed with the highest virtues, this son of the king was honoured among the people, respected in all three worlds for his earth-like quality of forbearance, equal to Bṛhaspati in wisdom, and equal to the lord of Śacī in valour.

sanskrit: tathā sarvaprajākāntaiḥ prītisaṃjananaiḥ pituḥ guṇair viruruce rāmo dīptaḥ sūrya ivāṃśubhiḥ
english: And so Rāma shone forth with virtues that were dear to all people and that inspired the father's love, blazing like the sun in his rays.

sanskrit: tam evaṃvṛttasaṃpannam apradhṛṣya parākramam lokapālopamaṃ nātham akāmayata medinī
english: The earth itself desired him as her lord — him who was endowed with such conduct and character, whose valour was irresistible, who was comparable to the guardians of the worlds.

sanskrit: etais tu bahubhir yuktaṃ guṇair anupamaiḥ sutam dṛṣṭvā daśaratho rājā cakre cintāṃ paraṃtapaḥ
english: Beholding his son endowed with these many incomparable virtues, king Daśaratha, that scorcher of foes, fell to pondering deeply.

sanskrit: eṣā hy asya parā prītir hṛdi saṃparivartate kadā nāma sutaṃ drakṣyāmy abhiṣiktam ahaṃ priyam
english: "This supreme joy that revolves within my heart — when indeed shall I behold my beloved son anointed as crown prince?"

sanskrit: vṛddhikāmo hi lokasya sarvabhūtānukampanaḥ mattaḥ priyataro loke parjanya iva vṛṣṭimān
english: "For he desires the welfare of the world, he has compassion for all beings, and he is dearer to the world than I am — like rain-bearing Parjanya is dearer than those who receive his rain."

sanskrit: yamaśakrasamo vīrye bṛhaspatisamo matau mahīdharasamo dhṛtyāṃ mattaś ca guṇavattaraḥ
english: "Equal to Yama and Śakra in valour, equal to Bṛhaspati in wisdom, equal to a mountain in steadfastness — and yet surpassing even me in virtue."

sanskrit: mahīm aham imāṃ kṛtsnām adhitiṣṭhantam ātmajam anena vayasā dṛṣṭvā yathā svargam avāpnuyām
english: "Having seen my own son governing this entire earth, and at this age, may I thereby attain to heaven."

sanskrit: taṃ samīkṣya mahārājo yuktaṃ samuditair guṇaiḥ niścitya sacivaiḥ sārdhaṃ yuvarājam amanyata
english: Considering him to be endowed with all these gathered virtues, the great king deliberated with his ministers and resolved to appoint him crown prince.

sanskrit: nānānagaravāstavyān pṛthagjānapadān api samānināya medinyāḥ pradhānān pṛthivīpatiḥ
english: The lord of the earth summoned the chief men dwelling in many different cities and separate provinces of the land.

sanskrit: atha rājavitīrṇeṣu vividheṣu āsaneṣu ca rājānam evābhimukhā niṣedur niyatā nṛpāḥ
english: Then upon the various seats distributed by the king's command, the assembled kings took their places, facing toward the king himself.

sanskrit: sa labdhamānair vinayānvitair nṛpaiḥ purālayair jānapadaiś ca mānavaiḥ upopaviṣṭair nṛpatir vṛto babhau sahasracakṣur bhagavān ivāmaraiḥ
english: The king shone forth, surrounded by those honoured and humble kings, the dwellers in cities, and the men from the provinces seated nearby — even as the blessed thousand-eyed Indra shines surrounded by the immortals.

sanskrit: tataḥ pariṣadaṃ sarvām āmantrya vasudhādhipaḥ hitam uddharṣaṇaṃ cedam uvācāpratimaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then the lord of the earth addressed the entire assembly and spoke this unequalled speech, beneficial and heartening.

sanskrit: dundubhisvanakalpena gambhīreṇānunādinā svareṇa mahatā rājā jīgmūta iva nādayan
english: With his great voice, deep and reverberating like the sound of a kettledrum, the king thundered like a rain-cloud.

sanskrit: so 'ham ikṣvākubhiḥ pūrvair narendraiḥ paripālitam śreyasā yoktukāmo 'smi sukhārham akhilaṃ jagat
english: "I, who have guarded this world that was protected by the former kings of the Ikṣvāku line, now desire to yoke it to greater prosperity — this entire world that is worthy of happiness."

sanskrit: mayāpy ācaritaṃ pūrvaiḥ panthānam anugacchatā prajā nityam atandreṇa yathāśakty abhirakṣatā
english: "By me also, following the path walked by those of old, the subjects have been protected constantly, without fatigue, to the full extent of my power."

sanskrit: idaṃ śarīraṃ kṛtsnasya lokasya caratā hitam pāṇḍur asyātapatrasyac chāyāyāṃ jaritaṃ mayā
english: "This body of mine has grown old in the shade of this white royal umbrella, while I wandered about for the welfare of the whole world."

sanskrit: prāpya varṣasahasrāṇi bahūny āyūṃṣi jīvitaḥ jīrṇasyāsya śarīrasya viśrāntim abhirocaye
english: "Having lived many thousands of years of life, I now desire rest for this aged body of mine."

sanskrit: rājaprabhāvajuṣṭāṃ hi durvahām ajitendriyaiḥ pariśrānto 'smi lokasya gurvīṃ dharmadhuraṃ vahan
english: "I am weary from bearing this heavy burden of dharma for the world — a burden invested with royal dignity, difficult to carry for those who have not conquered their senses."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ viśramam icchāmi putraṃ kṛtvā prajāhite saṃnikṛṣṭān imān sarvān anumānya dvijarṣabhān
english: "Thus I desire rest, having set my son in care of the people, and with the assent of all these eminent twice-born men assembled here."

sanskrit: anujāto hi me sarvair guṇair jyeṣṭho mamātmajaḥ puraṃdarasamo vīrye rāmaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: "For my eldest son has been born with all my virtues — Rāma, equal to Purandara in valour, the conqueror of enemy citadels."

sanskrit: taṃ candram iva puṣyeṇa yuktaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ varam yauvarājyena yoktāsmi prītaḥ puruṣapuṃgavam
english: "With joy I intend to invest that best of those who uphold dharma, that bull among men, with the dignity of crown prince — even as the moon is joined with the asterism Puṣya."

sanskrit: anurūpaḥ sa vo nātho lakṣmīvāṃl lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ trailokyam api nāthena yena syān nāthavattaram
english: "That lord of fortune, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa, is a fitting master for you — one by whose lordship even the three worlds would be better governed."

sanskrit: anena śreyasā sadyaḥ saṃyojyāham imāṃ mahīm gatakleśo bhaviṣyāmi sute tasmin niveśya vai
english: "Having forthwith yoked this earth to this greater good, and having entrusted it to that son, I shall be free of toil."

sanskrit: iti bruvantaṃ muditāḥ pratyanandan nṛpā nṛpam vṛṣṭimantaṃ mahāmeghaṃ nardantam iva barhiṇaḥ
english: The assembled kings, joyful, applauded the king as he spoke thus — like peacocks crying out in acclaim of a great rain-bearing cloud that thunders.

sanskrit: tasya dharmārthaviduṣo bhāvam ājñāya sarvaśaḥ ūcuś ca manasā jñātvā vṛddhaṃ daśarathaṃ nṛpam
english: Having understood in full the intent of that king who was learned in dharma and artha, and having known the aged king Daśaratha's mind, they said:

sanskrit: anekavarṣasāhasro vṛddhas tvam asi pārthiva sa rāmaṃ yuvarājānam abhiṣiñcasva pārthivam
english: "O king, you are aged, having lived many thousands of years; therefore anoint Rāma as crown prince, O lord of the earth."

sanskrit: iti tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rājā teṣāṃ manaḥpriyam ajānann iva jijñāsur idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Having heard those words pleasing to their hearts, the king, as if wishing to enquire further and not yet knowing their full mind, spoke these words.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu mayi dharmeṇa pṛthivīm anuśāsati bhavanto draṣṭum icchanti yuvarājaṃ mamātmajam
english: "How is it that while I am righteously governing the earth, you all wish to see my son as crown prince?"

sanskrit: te tam ūcur mahātmānaṃ paurajānapadaiḥ saha bahavo nṛpa kalyāṇā guṇāḥ putrasya santi te
english: They, along with the citizens and the people of the provinces, addressed that great-souled king: "O king, your son possesses many auspicious virtues."

sanskrit: divyair guṇaiḥ śakrasamo rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ ikṣvākubhyo hi sarvebhyo 'py atirakto viśāmpate
english: "Rāma, equal to Śakra in divine qualities and true in his valour, surpasses indeed all the Ikṣvākus, O lord of the people."

sanskrit: rāmaḥ satpuruṣo loke satyadharmaparāyaṇaḥ dharmajñaḥ satyasaṃdhaś ca śīlavān anasūyakaḥ
english: "Rāma is a good man in the world, devoted to true dharma, knowing righteousness, true to his word, of excellent character, and free from envy."

sanskrit: kṣāntaḥ sāntvayitā ślakṣṇaḥ kṛtajño vijitendriyaḥ mṛduś ca sthiracittaś ca sadā bhavyo 'nasūyakaḥ
english: "He is forbearing, a conciliator, gentle, grateful, master of his senses, soft-spoken, firm of mind, ever auspicious, and without envy."

sanskrit: priyavādī ca bhūtānāṃ satyavādī ca rāghavaḥ bahuśrutānāṃ vṛddhānāṃ brāhmaṇānām upāsitā
english: "That Rāghava speaks kindly to all beings and speaks the truth; he is an attendant upon brāhmaṇas who are greatly learned and advanced in age."

sanskrit: tenāsyehātulā kīrtir yaśas tejaś ca vardhate devāsuramanuṣyāṇāṃ sarvāstreṣu viśāradaḥ
english: "By reason of this, his incomparable glory, fame, and splendour grow here; and he is proficient in all the weapons of gods, asuras, and men."

sanskrit: yadā vrajati saṃgrāmaṃ grāmārthe nagarasya vā gatvā saumitrisahito nāvijitya nivartate
english: "Whenever he goes into battle for the sake of a village or the city, going along with Saumitri (Lakṣmaṇa), he never returns without victory."

sanskrit: saṃgrāmāt punar āgamya kuñjareṇa rathena vā paurān svajanavan nityaṃ kuśalaṃ paripṛcchati
english: "Returning from battle, whether on elephant or chariot, he always enquires after the welfare of the townspeople as though they were his own kin."

sanskrit: putreṣv agniṣu dāreṣu preṣyaśiṣyagaṇeṣu ca nikhilenānupūrvyā ca pitā putrān ivaurasān
english: "Regarding their sons, sacred fires, wives, servants and pupils — fully, in proper order, like a father with his own born sons."

sanskrit: śuśrūṣante ca vaḥ śiṣyāḥ kaccit karmasu daṃśitāḥ iti naḥ puruṣavyāghraḥ sadā rāmo 'bhibhāṣate
english: "'Are your pupils diligently attending you, equipped for their duties?' — thus that tiger among men, Rāma, always addresses us."

sanskrit: vyasaneṣu manuṣyāṇāṃ bhṛśaṃ bhavati duḥkhitaḥ utsaveṣu ca sarveṣu piteva parituṣyati
english: "In the misfortunes of men he is greatly grieved, and at all their festivals he rejoices like a father."

sanskrit: satyavādī maheṣvāso vṛddhasevī jitendriyaḥ vatsaḥ śreyasi jātas te diṣṭyāsau tava rāghavaḥ diṣṭyā putraguṇair yukto mārīca iva kaśyapaḥ
english: "A speaker of truth, a great bowman, a servant of elders, master of his senses — by good fortune this Rāghava has been born as your son in a good hour; by good fortune you, endowed with the virtues of your son, are like Kaśyapa blessed with Mārīca."

sanskrit: balam ārogyam āyuś ca rāmasya viditātmanaḥ āśaṃsate janaḥ sarvo rāṣṭre puravare tathā
english: "All the people in the kingdom and in the royal city pray for the strength, health, and long life of Rāma, that self-knowing one."

sanskrit: abhyantaraś ca bāhyaś ca paurajānapado janaḥ striyo vṛddhās taruṇyaś ca sāyaṃprātaḥ samāhitāḥ
english: "The people of the inner and outer city, the town-dwellers and villagers, women old and young, morning and evening with concentrated mind —"

sanskrit: sarvān devān namasyanti rāmasyārthe yaśasvinaḥ teṣām āyācitaṃ deva tvatprasādāt samṛdhyatām
english: "— they bow in reverence to all the gods for the sake of the glorious Rāma; O lord, may their prayers be fulfilled by your grace."

sanskrit: rāmam indīvaraśyāmaṃ sarvaśatrunibarhaṇam paśyāmo yauvarājyasthaṃ tava rājottamātmajam
english: "We wish to see Rāma, dark-complexioned as the blue lotus, the vanquisher of all enemies, your best of sons, established as crown prince."

sanskrit: taṃ devadevopamam ātmajaṃ te sarvasya lokasya hite niviṣṭam hitāya naḥ kṣipram udārajuṣṭaṃ mudābhiṣektuṃ varada tvam arhasi
english: "That son of yours, who is like unto the god of gods, who is devoted to the welfare of all the world — you, O granter of boons, should swiftly and joyfully anoint him who is endowed with nobility, for our own welfare."

sanskrit: teṣām ajñalipadmāni pragṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ pratigṛhyābravīd rājā tebhyaḥ priyahitaṃ vacaḥ
english: Having received from all of them their lotus-like folded hands raised in salutation, the king spoke words both pleasing and beneficial to them.

sanskrit: aho 'smi paramaprītaḥ prabhāvaś cātulo mama yan me jyeṣṭhaṃ priyaṃ putraṃ yauvarājyastham icchatha
english: "Ah, I am supremely delighted, and my majesty is unequalled, in that you desire my dear eldest son to be installed as crown prince."

sanskrit: iti pratyarcya tān rājā brāhmaṇān idam abravīt vasiṣṭhaṃ vāmadevaṃ ca teṣām evopaśṛṇvatām
english: Having thus honoured them in return, the king spoke these words to the brāhmaṇas, to Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva, while those same men listened.

sanskrit: caitraḥ śrīmān ayaṃ māsaḥ puṇyaḥ puṣpitakānanaḥ yauvarājyāya rāmasya sarvam evopakalpyatām
english: "This auspicious month of Caitra, sacred and with forests in full bloom — let everything be made ready for the installation of Rāma as crown prince."

sanskrit: kṛtam ity eva cābrūtām abhigamya jagatpatim yathoktavacanaṃ prītau harṣayuktau dvijarṣabhau
english: "It shall be done" — so said those two foremost of twice-born men, Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva, approaching the lord of the world, pleased and filled with joy, in accordance with his spoken command.

sanskrit: tataḥ sumantraṃ dyutimān rājā vacanam abravīt rāmaḥ kṛtātmā bhavatā śīghram ānīyatām iti
english: Then the radiant king spoke to Sumantra: "Let Rāma, that pure-souled one, be brought here by you swiftly."

sanskrit: sa tatheti pratijñāya sumantro rājaśāsanāt rāmaṃ tatrānayāṃ cakre rathena rathināṃ varam
english: Sumantra, having promised "So be it" and acting on the king's command, brought Rāma, the best of chariot-warriors, there by chariot.

sanskrit: atha tatra samāsīnās tadā daśarathaṃ nṛpam prācyodīcyāḥ pratīcyāś ca dākṣiṇātyāś ca bhūmipāḥ
english: Then the kings from the east, north, west, and south who were seated there around king Daśaratha —

sanskrit: mlecchāś cāryāś ca ye cānye vanaśailāntavāsinaḥ upāsāṃ cakrire sarve taṃ devā iva vāsavam
english: — and the Mlecchas and the Āryas and all others who dwelt in forests and mountain borders — all waited upon him as the gods wait upon Vāsava (Indra).

sanskrit: teṣāṃ madhye sa rājarṣir marutām iva vāsavaḥ prāsādastho rathagataṃ dadarśāyāntam ātmajam
english: That royal seer, standing in his palace among them like Vāsava among the Maruts, saw his son coming on the chariot.

sanskrit: gandharvarājapratimaṃ loke vikhyātapauruṣam dīrghabāhuṃ mahāsattvaṃ mattamātaṅgagāminam
english: — like unto the king of the Gandharvas, of renowned valour in the world, long-armed, of great being, walking with the gait of a rutting elephant —

sanskrit: candrakāntānanaṃ rāmam atīva priyadarśanam rūpaudāryaguṇaiḥ puṃsāṃ dṛṣṭicittāpahāriṇam
english: — Rāma, whose face was fair as the moon, exceedingly pleasing to behold, whose beauty, nobility, and virtues stole away the eyes and minds of men —

sanskrit: gharmābhitaptāḥ parjanyaṃ hlādayantam iva prajāḥ na tatarpa samāyāntaṃ paśyamāno narādhipaḥ
english: — like rain-bearing Parjanya gladdening people scorched by summer heat — the lord of men, gazing upon him as he approached, was not satiated.

sanskrit: avatārya sumantras taṃ rāghavaṃ syandanottamāt pituḥ samīpaṃ gacchantaṃ prāñjaliḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nvagāt
english: Sumantra, having helped that Rāghava down from the excellent chariot, followed him with joined palms as he walked toward his father's presence.

sanskrit: sa taṃ kailāsaśṛṅgābhaṃ prāsādaṃ narapuṃgavaḥ āruroha nṛpaṃ draṣṭuṃ saha sūtena rāghavaḥ
english: That bull among men, that Rāghava, ascended the palace that gleamed like the peak of Kailāsa to see his father, accompanied by the charioteer.

sanskrit: sa prāñjalir abhipretya praṇataḥ pitur antike nāma svaṃ śrāvayan rāmo vavande caraṇau pituḥ
english: Approaching with joined palms, bowing low near his father, causing his own name to be announced, Rāma reverenced his father's feet.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā praṇataṃ pārśve kṛtāñjalipuṭaṃ nṛpaḥ gṛhyāñjalau samākṛṣya sasvaje priyam ātmajam
english: Seeing him bowed at his side with joined palms, the king took his hands, drew him close, and embraced his beloved son.

sanskrit: tasmai cābhyudyataṃ śrīmān maṇikāñcanabhūṣitam dideśa rājā ruciraṃ rāmāya paramāsanam
english: And the glorious king directed Rāma to that excellent seat of honour which had been brought forward, adorned with gems and gold.

sanskrit: tad āsanavaraṃ prāpya vyadīpayata rāghavaḥ svayeva prabhayā merum udaye vimalo raviḥ
english: Having taken that best of seats, Rāghava illumined it by his own radiance, as the pure sun at its rising illumines Mount Meru.

sanskrit: tena vibhrājitā tatra sā sabhābhivyarocata vimalagrahanakṣatrā śāradī dyaur ivendunā
english: Illumined by him, the assembly hall shone forth splendidly — like the autumnal sky, clear of planets and stars, shining by the moon.

sanskrit: taṃ paśyamāno nṛpatis tutoṣa priyam ātmajam alaṃkṛtam ivātmānam ādarśatalasaṃsthitam
english: Gazing upon his beloved son, the king was pleased, as if beholding his own adorned self placed in the surface of a mirror.

sanskrit: sa taṃ sasmitam ābhāṣya putraṃ putravatāṃ varaḥ uvācedaṃ vaco rājā devendram iva kaśyapaḥ
english: Addressing his son with a smile, the king, best of those who have sons, spoke these words — like Kaśyapa addressing the lord of the gods.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhāyām asi me patnyāṃ sadṛśyāṃ sadṛśaḥ sutaḥ utpannas tvaṃ guṇaśreṣṭho mama rāmātmajaḥ priyaḥ
english: "You are a fitting son born of my foremost wife who is fit for you; you have arisen as my dearest son Rāma, excelling in virtue, born of my own self."

sanskrit: tvayā yataḥ prajāś cemāḥ svaguṇair anurañjitāḥ tasmāt tvaṃ puṣyayogena yauvarājyam avāpnuhi
english: "Since these subjects are won over by your own virtues, therefore you shall receive the dignity of crown prince under the asterism Puṣya."

sanskrit: kāmatas tvaṃ prakṛtyaiva vinīto guṇavān asi guṇavaty api tu snehāt putra vakṣyāmi te hitam
english: "By your very nature you are disciplined and virtuous of your own accord; yet even to one already virtuous, I shall speak what is beneficial for you, out of affection, my son."

sanskrit: bhūyo vinayam āsthāya bhava nityaṃ jitendriyaḥ kāmakrodhasamutthāni tyajethā vyasanāni ca
english: "Cultivating humility still more, be always master of your senses; and abandon the vices that arise from desire and anger."

sanskrit: parokṣayā vartamāno vṛttyā pratyakṣayā tathā amātyaprabhṛtīḥ sarvāḥ prakṛtīś cānurañjaya
english: "Whether acting in matters seen or unseen, win the affection of all the constituents of the state, beginning with the ministers."

sanskrit: tuṣṭānuraktaprakṛtir yaḥ pālayati medinīm tasya nandanti mitrāṇi labdhvāmṛtam ivāmarāḥ tasmāt putra tvam ātmānaṃ niyamyaiva samācara
english: "He who governs the earth with satisfied and devoted subjects — his allies rejoice as the immortals rejoice on obtaining ambrosia. Therefore, my son, conduct yourself only after restraining your own self."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā suhṛdas tasya rāmasya priyakāriṇaḥ tvaritāḥ śīghram abhyetya kausalyāyai nyavedayan
english: Having heard this, the friends of Rāma who loved to do him service hastened swiftly and went to announce the news to Kausalyā.

sanskrit: sā hiraṇyaṃ ca gāś caiva ratnāni vividhāni ca vyādideśa priyākhyebhyaḥ kausalyā pramadottamā
english: That best of women, Kausalyā, distributed gold, cows, and various jewels to those who had brought her the glad tidings.

sanskrit: athābhivādya rājānaṃ ratham āruhya rāghavaḥ yayau svaṃ dyutimad veśma janaughaiḥ pratipūjitaḥ
english: Then, having paid his respects to the king, Rāghava mounted the chariot and departed to his own radiant dwelling, honoured by the throngs of people.

sanskrit: te cāpi paurā nṛpater vacas tac chrutvā tadā lābham iveṣṭam āpya narendram āmantya gṛhāṇi gatvā devān samānarcur atīva hṛṣṭāḥ
english: And the townspeople too, having heard that word of the king, as if obtaining a cherished gain, took leave of the lord of men and went to their homes, and worshipped the gods with exceeding joy.
